queries.Our core methodological innovation invol: Transformer-based multi-agent reinforcement learning for traffic signal control using inter-agent communication, 2D positional encoding from normalized longitude and latitude, spatial attention, and enriched agent states for coordinating intersections with minimal traffic observations
queries.We will model TSC optimization as a mult: multi-agent Markov decision process formulation for traffic signal control with decentralized intersection agents, local proximity observations, and a shared global reward
queries.We will optimize the value function and: Proximal Policy Optimization for multi-agent traffic signal control, training value function and policy with traffic light phase change actions and rewards from vehicle waiting time differences in SUMO
queries.We will design three levels of state obs: multi-agent reinforcement learning traffic signal control with variable state observation levels: no traffic observation using only traffic light information, limited high-level map metrics, and full detailed sensor data, evaluating minimal state information for competitive performance
queries.We will use a PointNet-inspired encoder: PointNet-inspired permutation-invariant encoder with shared MLP weights and max-pooling for canonical lane-level representations of heterogeneous intersection geometries in multi-agent traffic signal control
queries.We will implement attention-based commun: Transformer-based inter-agent communication for multi-agent traffic signal control, where agents attend to other intersection states using exponential distance-decayed attention masking and 2D spatial positional encoding.
queries.We will conduct comprehensive experiment: SUMO simulation experiments for multi-agent traffic signal control using transformer communication, PPO, dynamic traffic flow, network complexity, state information levels, waiting time, travel time, queue length, emissions, and fuel consumption
queries.We will train both our transformer model: Training a transformer multi-agent reinforcement learning model and a simple MLP baseline for traffic signal control on a seven-agent ring network with static traffic flow in SUMO, comparing convergence and performance across different levels of state information availability.
queries.We will evaluate our transformer model o: Transformer-based multi-agent reinforcement learning for traffic signal control in SUMO on a 73-intersection grid network with dynamic time-varying traffic flow, evaluating scalability and robustness across full, limited, and no traffic state observations.
queries.We will implement and test our automated: Automated pipeline for generating randomized road networks and traffic demand scenarios in SUMO for multi-agent reinforcement learning traffic signal control, sampling environments conditioned on number of intersections and average traffic density to create scalable synthetic training data without real-world traffic data
queries.We will simultaneously train our model o: Unified multi-agent reinforcement learning model for traffic signal control trained simultaneously on multiple road networks of varying complexity to generalize across diverse topologies, traffic demands, and variable input sizes using transformer-based inter-agent communication.
queries.We will evaluate our trained models on b: Generalization of multi-agent reinforcement learning traffic signal control from synthetic road networks to real-world road networks in SUMO, evaluating transfer performance with waiting time, travel time, queue length, fuel consumption, and CO2 emissions across varying network topologies.
queries.We will compare our models against stati: Evaluating multi-agent reinforcement learning traffic signal control in SUMO with one-hour simulations, measuring fuel consumption, CO2 emissions, waiting vehicles, travel time, queue length, and delay against static control baselines
queries.The experiments will systematically vary: multi-agent reinforcement learning traffic signal control experiments that vary network complexity, dynamic traffic flow, and state information availability to evaluate transformer-based inter-agent communication and minimal state observations in SUMO simulations
